fixes.explanation: It's true. God says of Jerusalem, “They cling to deceit; they refuse to return.” The word is refuse, and God says it right there. I've had a cookie sheet that wouldn't budge from the rack, but that's nothing next to this.

God says, “They cling to deceit…” Cling means a tight grip, like hanging on to the last cookie in the box while everybody stares at you. Right after that He says, “…they refuse to return.” Deceit is the answer in this verse.

God says, “Everyone has pursued his own course like a horse charging into battle.” Picture that horse charging into battle. That's the picture God picks for everyone pursuing his own course. And in the same verse, nobody is asking, “What have I done?”

Sheep wandering is a gentle picture, a little lost and a little clueless. God uses a much louder one here. He says they pursue their own course “…like a horse charging into battle.” That's a very different picture from sheep on a hill.

God says “…the lying pen of the scribes has produced a deception?” The scribes were the writers, and here the pen itself is called a liar. The people said, “We are wise…” and God says that pen produced a deception. I'd be embarrassed if my stamp did that to a cookie.

House is an interesting pick, but this verse isn't about a building. God says they dress the wound of His people with very little care. The wound is what gets dressed, and the words they say are “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace at all.

God says, “Whatever I have given them will be lost to them.” That comes right after He says He will take away their harvest, with no grapes on the vine and no figs on the tree. Everything He had given them would be lost to them. Lost is the word.

The voices say, “Gather together, let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there…” Fortified cities are cities built with strong defenses. That's where they propose to go, and they say they will perish there. That's a heavy line, so I think it hurts to read.

The voices say, “…the LORD our God has doomed us. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.” They name the reason right there in the verse. They say it's because they have sinned against the LORD. True is the answer.
It's true. These voices say, “He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.” They say it right there in the verse. So the answer is True.
Silence might feel like the quiet after a letdown. But the voices say, “…for a time of healing, but there was only terror.” What came was terror. Silence isn't in the verse.

The voices say, “The snorting of enemy horses is heard from Dan. At the sound of the neighing of mighty steeds, the whole land quakes.” Snorting and neighing are the sounds. The whole land quakes at the sound. Imagine that.
God says, “…I will send snakes among you, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you…” These vipers cannot be charmed. And they will bite. Both parts are right there in the verse.
The verse doesn't limit it that way. God says, “…I will send snakes among you, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you…” The word is you. No leaders-only rule is in the text.
